title: ChartLab — Mark the Zone
data_notice: Illustrative teaching data only; not live or real-market historical data.
general_principles: Support and resistance zones represent areas where price previously reacted; they do not create the reaction or guarantee a future move.
Reference zones are teaching anchors, not exact-price grading targets.
Assess support and resistance separately; feedback must address structure location, coverage, zone width, reasoning and a next action.
Do not treat the W-shape as an automatic entry signal or guaranteed bullish reversal.

evaluation_dimensions.question: Is the zone on the relevant part of structure?
evaluation_dimensions.support: Around both troughs, not just one low.
evaluation_dimensions.resistance: Around the intervening recovery high/neckline, not later highs.

evaluation_dimensions.question: Does it capture the relevant reaction cluster?
evaluation_dimensions.guidance: Allow reasonable boundary differences; don't require exact pixel overlap.

evaluation_dimensions.question: Is the zone useful without being too broad?
evaluation_dimensions.guidance: Support and resistance may have different widths. Each width should be justified by its own price behaviour.

evaluation_dimensions.question: Does the learner point to observable chart evidence?
evaluation_dimensions.guidance: Reward reference to repeated reactions, wick/body variation, swing highs/lows and the neckline; challenge claims of guaranteed reversals.

studies.name: Clear W
studies.objective: Identify two troughs and the intervening recovery high as two distinct areas of interest.

support.evidence: Two prominent trough wicks approximately 99.15 and 98.70.

support.width_guidance: Keep the band focused while representing both trough reactions.

resistance.width_guidance: Capture the neckline, not the later highs.

rationale.support: Repeated reactions occur in a similar low area, but not at one exact price. The zone should cover both troughs without swallowing unrelated price action.
rationale.resistance: The recovery between the troughs reaches a local high and backs away; this is the neckline area.
rationale.caution: The W and the zones do not guarantee a bullish continuation.

q1.correct: Support surrounds the two troughs; resistance marks the intervening swing high, or neckline.

misconceptions.exact: Zones are areas, not exact prices that force reversals.
misconceptions.signal: Zones alone do not confirm a buy or sell entry.

q2.correct: Price moved above the prior resistance area; follow-through remains uncertain.

misconceptions.continue: A close above resistance does not guarantee continuation.
misconceptions.support: Support is not guaranteed to hold on a future return.

studies.name: Uneven lows
studies.objective: Accommodate a deeper second trough without making support indiscriminately wide.

support.width_guidance: Both trough reactions must remain represented; avoid unrelated price action.

resistance.width_guidance: Do not automatically widen resistance to match support.

rationale.support: The second trough reaches lower, so a thin band around only the first low omits part of the structure. The wider band remains anchored to the two lows.
rationale.resistance: Resistance remains the intervening recovery high; its width is determined independently from support.
rationale.caution: An uneven low neither proves failure nor confirms a reversal.

q1.correct: Support may be wider because the two lows are less even and the second probe is deeper.

q2.correct: No. Each zone's width should reflect its own price behaviour.

q3.correct: No. The deeper second trough changes the evidence but does not guarantee the next move.

studies.name: Wider neckline
studies.objective: Represent a broader recovery/hesitation band while keeping support focused on the troughs.

resistance.evidence: Broader intervening recovery high, local high approximately 106.7.

support.width_guidance: Keep support anchored to the low cluster.

resistance.width_guidance: Capture the broader recovery cluster without expanding into unrelated prices.

rationale.support: Both troughs remain in a focused low area; do not widen support just because resistance is broader.
rationale.resistance: The recovery hesitates across a wider area, so a band conveys the visible variation better than a precise line.
rationale.caution: A broader neckline does not guarantee breakout or rejection.

q1.correct: Resistance is wider because the recovery high and hesitation span a broader area.

q2.correct: No. Each zone reflects its own reaction cluster.

q3.correct: No. The zone represents an area to observe, not a prediction.
